newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - EU Stability pact boosts European markets.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EU Stability pact boosts European markets.

text.p: European financial markets strove to put last week's volatility behind them on Monday as major bourses, bonds and the dollar rose following agreement on an EU stability pact.
Agreement between EU leaders in Dublin on a mechanism for ensuring monetary discipline after the launch of a single currency in 1999 boosted bond markets and the dollar.

That, in turn, helped stock markets begin the week with a sharp rise following the gyrations of recent days, although the mood remained cautious ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee, which sets U.S. interest rates.
The Dublin stability deal pact was seen by the foreign exchange market as weakening sentiment on the mark and the dollar rose more than half a pfennig in early European trade.

Analysts said the pact bolstered optimism that Europe's single currrency project would go ahead on time in 1999 and increased the chance of a broad-based monetary union that would include Italy and Spain.
The pact was also seen lowering the European interest rate horizon, buoying both the dollar and yen against European currencies.
"The initial market reaction to the stability pact has been been negative for the mark and this is totally justified in my opinion," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
Government bond markets gained on the news from Dublin, with German bunds getting an added boost from an unexpected dip in an influential German business confidence index.
The IFO index, considered a key barometer of the German business climate, dropped to 96.9 in November from a revised 97.3 in October.

Europe's major stock markets -- London, Paris and Frankfurt -- all shot higher at the start, although traders said they remained vulnerable to the sort of volatility sparked by Wall Street over the past 10 days.
"Investors are still holding back a bit. Some think there is room for a correction down to 2,750," one Frankfurt dealer said after the DAX Index made a strong start.
The 30-share DAX index zoomed more 45 points, or 1.6 percent, in early trade to stand at 2,844.56 by 1015 GMT.

Wall Street's recovery on Friday from big losses to end one point up was seen supporting European bourses, which have been watching U.S. markets closely since Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan caused turmoil earlier this month with his comments about "irrational exuberance".
Europe's largest equity market, London, climbed in early business, dragged upwards by strong bond futures, the stability pact and Wall Street.
The FTSE 100 was up 19 points at 3,991 by 1015 GMT, with some traders saying the market might yet experience its traditional year-end rally.
British Aerospace lost a modest early gain after news of the merger agreement between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas. By 1015 GMT it was down 9.5p at 1,115p.

News of a bid approach for Newman Tonks from FKI as well as a merger agreement between insurance brokers JIB Group and Lloyds Thompson could revived the bid talk that has boosted the market this year.
"If there are plenty of bids around that's what the market is going to focus on," said one head of equity trading. "All the speculation has a habit of feeding on itself."
French shares opened sharply higher after Friday's fall, like other European bourses gaining from the rise in bond futures.
Despite that, traders said they expected investors to remain cautious ahead of monetary meetings this week in France, the United States and Germany.
Luxury goods trader LVMH was the biggest early gainer on the CAC-40 index, rising 2.38 percent to 1,288 before slipping back a bit.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5551 marks and 113.87 yen compared with 1.5473 marks and 113.95 yen in late European business on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of top British shares was up 19.1 points at 3,991.5
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 19.95 points at 2,223.36.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX was up 44.85 points at 2,844.56.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened at $368.30 an ounce, down from $369.80 at the close in London on Friday. Silver began two cents lower at $4.81.
